cards.title: Saudi Rank and Respect
cards.body: Saudi officers value hierarchy. Address them by their rank and last name. They expect deference and respect. Use titles like 'Colonel' or 'General' followed by their name. Avoid familiarity until invited.
doThis: Address seniors by their rank and last name

source.doc: AFCLC Expeditionary Culture Field Guide: Saudi Arabia (2025)

cards.title: Qatari Rank Etiquette
cards.body: Qatari officers appreciate respect for rank. Use their full rank and name initially. They may invite you to use their first name later. Maintain a polite and formal demeanor. Avoid public criticism or disagreement.
doThis: Use full rank and name initially

source.doc: AFCLC Expeditionary Culture Field Guide: Saudi Arabia (2025)

cards.title: Saudi Hospitality: Meals
cards.body: Meals are social events. Eat with your right hand. Say 'Bismillah' before and 'Al-hamdu lillah' after. Share dishes family-style. Avoid alcohol and pork. No left hand for food. Women may eat separately.
doThis: Use your right hand to eat.
avoidThis: Use your left hand for food.

source.doc: AFCLC Expeditionary Culture Field Guide: Saudi Arabia (2025)

cards.title: Qatari Hospitality: Coffee
cards.body: Coffee is a sign of respect. Accept at least one cup. Swivel your cup to signal you're done. Use right hand. No milk or sugar in traditional coffee. Avoid refusing outright.
doThis: Accept at least one cup of coffee.
Swivel your cup to signal you're finished.
avoidThis: Ask for milk or sugar in traditional coffee.

source.doc: AFCLC Expeditionary Culture Field Guide: Saudi Arabia (2025)

cards.title: Respect Hierarchy in Refusal
cards.body: In Saudi and Qatari cultures, hierarchy is important. When refusing a senior's request, show respect and maintain their dignity. Use indirect language and offer alternatives if possible.
doThis: Address seniors with their title and first name
Use indirect language (e.g., 'This may not be possible')

source.doc: AFCLC Expeditionary Culture Field Guide: Saudi Arabia (2025)

cards.title: Save Face in Refusal
cards.body: Both Saudis and Qataris value saving face. When refusing, be polite and considerate. Avoid direct confrontation and maintain a positive tone.
doThis: Use polite phrases (e.g., 'I'll try my best')

source.doc: AFCLC Expeditionary Culture Field Guide: Saudi Arabia (2025)

cards.title: Respecting Hierarchy in Saudi Arabia
cards.body: In Saudi culture, hierarchy is important. Address seniors with their title and first name, like 'Colonel Ahmed'. Avoid using only their first name or title alone. When disagreeing, do so privately and respectfully.
doThis: Use titles and first names for seniors
avoidThis: Use only first names or titles alone

source.doc: AFCLC Expeditionary Culture Field Guide: Saudi Arabia (2025)

cards.title: Qatari Communication Etiquette
cards.body: Qataris value politeness and indirect communication. Avoid saying 'no' directly; instead, use phrases like 'I'll try' or 'Insha'Allah'. Be mindful of personal space and avoid interrupting. Greet with a handshake, but wait for women to initiate.
doThis: Wait for women to initiate greetings
avoidThis: Initiate physical contact with opposite sex

source.doc: AFCLC Expeditionary Culture Field Guide: Saudi Arabia (2025)

cards.title: Respect Hierarchy in Saudi

cards.title: Qatari Time Flexibility
cards.body: Qataris have a relaxed approach to time. Meetings may start late. Be patient with delays. Avoid showing frustration to save face.

source.doc: AFCLC Expeditionary Culture Field Guide: Saudi Arabia (2025)

cards.title: Addressing Saudi Superiors
cards.body: In Saudi culture, hierarchy is important. Use titles and last names when addressing seniors. Avoid direct disagreement to save face. Women may not be present in all settings.
doThis: Use titles and last names for seniors
avoidThis: Expect women in all professional settings

source.doc: AFCLC Expeditionary Culture Field Guide: Saudi Arabia (2025)

cards.title: Qatari Checkpoint Etiquette
cards.body: At checkpoints, be patient and polite. Security staff may be male, but female officers are increasingly common. Avoid physical contact with opposite gender staff unless necessary.

source.doc: AFCLC Expeditionary Culture Field Guide: Saudi Arabia (2025)

cards.title: Respect Senior Officers
cards.body: Saudi and Qatari officers hold hierarchical positions due to cultural and religious norms. Show respect through formal addresses and actions. Avoid public criticism or disagreement.
doThis: Address seniors with their rank and title.
Avoid interrupting or contradicting them publicly.
avoidThis: Use first names or informal language with seniors.
Criticize or disagree openly with superiors.

source.doc: AFCLC Expeditionary Culture Field Guide: Saudi Arabia (2025)

cards.title: Handle Refusal Tactfully
cards.body: Saying 'no' directly can cause loss of face. Instead, Saudis and Qataris may use indirect language or silence. Be patient and understanding.

source.doc: AFCLC Expeditionary Culture Field Guide: Saudi Arabia (2025)

cards.title: Gift Giving to Saudis
cards.body: Gifts are appreciated but not expected. Present gifts with both hands. Avoid alcohol and pork products. Gifts are usually opened later, not in front of the giver. Hierarchy matters; give more valuable gifts to seniors.
avoidThis: Expect gifts to be opened immediately

source.doc: AFCLC Expeditionary Culture Field Guide: Saudi Arabia (2025)

cards.title: Gift Giving to Qataris
cards.body: Gifts are common in business and social settings. Present gifts with the right hand or both hands. Avoid overly expensive gifts to prevent embarrassment. Gifts are usually opened later. Hierarchy matters; give more valuable gifts to seniors.
avoidThis: Expect gifts to be opened immediately

source.doc: AFCLC Expeditionary Culture Field Guide: Saudi Arabia (2025)

cards.body: Meals are social events. Say 'Bismillah' before eating, 'Al-hamdu lillah' after. Use your right hand. Share dishes. Avoid pork and alcohol. Women may eat separately with male guests.

cards.title: Qatari Meal Etiquette
cards.body: Meals are communal. Say 'Bismillah' before eating, 'Al-hamdu lillah' after. Use your right hand. Share dishes. Avoid pork and alcohol. Tipping 10-15% in restaurants is appreciated.

cards.title: Navigate Checkpoints and Security
cards.body: Checkpoints and security staff are common. Carry identification at all times. Be patient and polite. Local nationals may assist but avoid discussing sensitive topics.
doThis: Be patient and polite with security staff
avoidThis: Discuss sensitive topics with local nationals

cards.title: Respect Hierarchy in Radio
cards.body: Saudi and Qatari officers value hierarchy. Address seniors with their rank and name. Avoid direct disagreement. Use indirect phrases like 'Perhaps we could consider...' to suggest alternatives.
doThis: Use full rank and name for seniors

source.doc: AFCLC Expeditionary Culture Field Guide: Saudi Arabia (2025)

cards.title: Radio Etiquette in Saudi, Qatar
cards.body: Speak clearly and politely. Avoid slang and informal language. Use 'please' and 'thank you'. Keep messages concise. Wait for a response before continuing.

source.doc: AFCLC Expeditionary Culture Field Guide: Saudi Arabia (2025)

cards.title: Hierarchy and Addressing Seniors
cards.body: Saudi and Qatari cultures value hierarchy. Address seniors with their title and last name. Use 'Your Excellency' for high-ranking officers. Avoid familiar language.

cards.title: Saving Face and Criticism
cards.body: Indirect communication is preferred. Criticism should be given privately and delicately. Avoid public disagreement or confrontation to maintain harmony.

cards.title: Rank and Addressing in Qatar
cards.body: Qatari ranks follow NATO standards. Address superiors by rank and name. Use 'Sheikh' for royal family members. Avoid familiarity with seniors.

cards.title: Qatari Hospitality and Meetings
cards.body: Qataris are warm hosts. Meetings may start late. Coffee and dates are often served. Avoid scheduling meetings during prayer times or Friday afternoons.
doThis: Accept coffee and dates as a sign of respect
